title: Man killed by Mounties sought revenge: Witness
article: Darby Mahon was protective of his grown daughter, but those who knew him never thought it would end up costing him his life.

Armed with a machete, Mahon left his third-floor apartment suite Wednesday evening and went to a first-floor suite to confront a man who had allegedly assaulted his daughter, believed to be in her mid 20s, said neighbour and witness Ferlin Aginas.

Instead, Mahon would be fatally shot by two Mounties from the Stony Plain RCMP detachment, who were called to the apartment around 7:30 p.m. after receiving a call about a disturbance in the Onoway apartment building on Lac Ste. Anne Trail.

Since the matter is now being investigated by the Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT), police are saying little about the shooting other than when the two members arrived at the apartment, they were confronted by a man with an edged weapon.
Aginas said Mahon, who lives above him, was armed with the machete and busted open the door of the basement level-suite to confront the man who he believed had assaulted his daughter.
That's when things turned violent.
"I heard a girl yelling and screaming, so I went down there. That was my first reaction - somebody is going to get hurt," said Aginas about the loud bang he heard downstairs before the yelling began.
He then called police.
"They (responding officers) heard him saying, 'I'm going to kill you. I'm not leaving this place until you're dead.' All he wanted was for the man to confront him."

Aginas went downstairs to investigate what was going on. He saw the door of the suite below him had been cracked wide open and Mahon was holding the weapon, still yelling at the man who he believed had locked himself in his room.
Aginas said he tried to calm Mahon down, but by the time police arrived, he was "still crazy, trying to hurt people."
Aginas went back to his apartment suite upstairs and heard four gun shots fired. Nobody left their suite after that, he said.

"It's unbelievable, to tell you the truth. I couldn't believe it. I went to sleep last night thinking maybe I had a bad dream," said Aginas, who wanted to intervene, but didn't at the advice of the building caretaker.
"I knew something was going to happen. If this young man would have faced what he did... they would have both been in custody, but this wouldn't have happened."
According to Aginas - and a friend of Mahon's who did not want to be identified - Mahon's daughter had moved in with him about two months ago with her baby.

Mahon's friend who did not want to be identified wasn't at home at the time of the shooting, but arrived at the apartment to find the road blocked off. He's still trying to understand why Mahon, believed to be in his mid-50s, was shot.
"He's really protective about his daughter and this little baby," said the man.
"He was a kind, decent person. He was a good friend."
Aginas didn't know Mahon very well, but said he was kind to the kids in the building and they often called him grandpa.
Kevin Koski, who lives on the second floor, wasn't aware of the events that unfolded in his building Wednesday evening until the army of police cars arrived at the scene.
He estimates around 17 cop cars came to the apartment building. That's when he knew something was terribly wrong.

"We were a little bit nervous to know what was going on," said Koski, who's lived in his apartment for about three years and noted there has been trouble in the building in the past, but nothing like this.
"It brings it close to home. It really makes you think."
ASIRT executive director, Clifton Purvis, couldn't confirm how many shots were fired other than "several" and said investigators are now waiting for the autopsy to be completed.
The Mountie's two firearms have been seized, along with a knife and a machete.
Purvis knew little about the officers, other than one of them had three years of service.
Onoway is about 70 km northwest of Edmonton.
